name: illustrator-internal-css-lower-third
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS
story: A news lower third - amber-ruled panel, reporter name, job title, city strap - exported with Internal CSS, Object IDs: Layer Names and Responsive ON, so the file has a viewBox and no width/height and every line is positioned by a matrix transform.
idioms: Generator comment: 'Adobe Illustrator 28.6.0, SVG Export Plug-In . SVG Version: 6.00 Build 0)'
root attrs in Illustrator's order: version="1.1" id="Layer_1" xmlns xmlns:xlink x="0px" y="0px", then viewBox on a continuation line indented with a tab and a space
Responsive ON: viewBox only, no width/height attributes
<style type="text/css"> block as a direct child of <svg> (not wrapped in <defs>), tab-indented
.st0/.st1/... single-purpose classes, one property each, uppercase hex fills
opacity emitted as its own class on a wrapper <g>: .st0{opacity:0.94;enable-background:new    ;} with the four-space padding Illustrator writes
PostScript face names in quotes: font-family:'Archivo-Bold', font-family:'Inter-Medium'
font-size in its own class, in px
_x20_ escape for a layer-name space: id="Job_x20_title" data-name="Job title"
_x5F_ escape for a literal underscore: id="BG_x5F_Panel" data-name="BG_Panel"
duplicate layer name uniquified as id="Name_1_" with data-name="Name" holding the original spelling
tab indentation, one tab per nesting level
whyThisMatters: Every position in this file lives in a matrix transform and every label lives behind an escape or a uniquify suffix, so an importer that reads x/y attributes or trusts the raw id finds no fields and shows the operator 'Job_x20_title' and 'Name_1_' - the exact two failures a designer meets on their very first Illustrator export.
